summary:
Harmonia is a burning-activity calendar that puts MODIS and VIIRS hotspot counts on one scale. The two satellites both detect active fires, but VIIRS sees more of them, and MODIS is leaving service. A higher count can be a new satellite, not a worse month.
The app uses NASA FIRMS detections for Argentina: MODIS Collection 6.1 Terra and Aqua, and VIIRS S-NPP Collection 2, from 20 January 2012 to 31 December 2025. Each VIIRS count is divided by that calendar month’s usual VIIRS-to-MODIS ratio. The overall median ratio is 3.507. A user picks Argentina, La Rioja, or Chilecito, then a month and a day, and sees whether that date is outside the record. The same place and month can be opened on NASA’s FIRMS map.
In August 2020, Argentina was 3.23 times a normal August. Chilecito, the same month, was quiet. The calendar still holds when the satellite changes.
details:
Harmonia is a web calendar for fire managers, scientists, and land managers. The user picks Argentina, La Rioja, or Chilecito, then a month and a day. The page shows that date across 2012–2025, a flag if it is outside the usual count, and a map of the month. A button opens the same place and month on NASA’s FIRMS map. That map is a check. The calendar numbers come from the downloaded files.

The science is a monthly ratio. VIIRS S-NPP counts are divided by the median VIIRS-to-MODIS ratio for that calendar month. The overall median is 3.507. The in-sample error is 6.0% on the same months, so it is not an independent test. August 2020 is the proof: Argentina is 37,479 harmonized, 3.23 times a normal August. Chilecito is 2 harmonized, 0.60 times, and inside normal.

It is a TypeScript web app. The counts were calculated in Python from the FIRMS archive. Column names follow NASA’s MODIS and VIIRS active-fire attributes. La Rioja and Chilecito are rectangles, not official borders. The file does not include years before 20 January 2012, burned area, or a fire that is burning right now.

Grok was used to help write the application code, the page text, and the seven-slide pitch. The hotspot counts, the ratio 3.507, the 6.0% error, and the August 2020 numbers were calculated from the team’s NASA FIRMS downloads. No NASA logo was generated.
